brief: The composition initially displays a rigid, meticulously structured typographic grid of bold black and white text, mimicking a formal exhibition poster. This rigid structure is never static; the perfect lines are continually destabilized, beginning to warp and melt. Over time, the typed elements break down, giving way to flowing, organic shapes that appear to be driven by immense, churning clockwork mechanisms and invisible gears. The resulting chaos is contained within the canvas, but interacting with the screen introduces a force that redirects and intensifies the breakdown process.

statement: This sketch depicts the slow erosion of a rigid ceramic floor structure into flowing sediment. Initially appearing as a grid of cleanly fractured tiles, the composition gradually dissolves and reorganizes into organic, overlapping fragments that accumulate like mineral deposits. The viewer witnesses the breakdown of a formal architectural element through time and interaction—each tile responds to contact with the cursor by breaking apart further, accelerating its dissolution into a flowing mass of sedimentary shapes. The piece explores how static structures gradually yield to natural forces, creating an ever-shifting landscape of fractured geometry that maintains visual coherence even as it degrades.
